thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Tech Leads Stock-market Rebound As Investors Watch U.S.-China Trade Spat

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Tech Leads Stock-market Rebound As Investors Watch U.S.-China Trade Spat
text:
By Barbara Kollmeyer, MarketWatch , Ryan Vlastelica
Trump tweets that he's optimistic China will make the right moves
U.S. stocks rallied on Monday, advancing in a broad move higher as comments from President Donald Trump and administration officials helped to ease concerns about the rise in trade hostilities between the U.S. and China.
What are main benchmarks doing?
The Dow Jones Industrial Averagewas recently up 270 points, or 1.1%, at 24,206. The S&P 500 added 31 points to 2,635, a gain of 1.2%. The Nasdaq Composite Indexrose 115 points, or 1.7%, to 7,030.
The day's gains were broad, with nine of the 11 primary S&P 500 sectors in positive territory. By far, the top-performing sector was technology, which surged 2.1%.
Major indexes have been volatile of late, with trade the major driver of moves in both directions. On Friday, trade concerns triggered sharp losses (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/dow-poised-for-over-200-point-drop-on-fresh-us-tariff-threat-as-jobs-data-looms-2018-04-06) that pushed the major indexes lower for the week.
Read:Stock-market bulls are looking for earnings to ride to the rescue (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/stock-market-bulls-are-looking-for-earnings-to-ride-to-the-rescue-2018-04-07)
What's driving markets
Signs that Trump may have softened his approach in a trade spat with China was lifting appetite for global equities across the board.
Optimism rose over the weekend after Trump alluded to hopes an agreement could be reached between the two nations on trade. "China will take down its Trade Barriers because it is the right thing to do. Taxes will become Reciprocal & a deal will be made on Intellectual Property," he tweeted.
(https://twitter.com/realDonaldTrump/status/982954355509907457)
In addition, administration officials made the rounds of Sunday talk shows (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/trump-administration-dials-down-the-rhetoric-on-china-tariffs-2018-04-08), playing down the possibility that the situation will escalate. Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin told CBS's "Face the Nation" that he doesn't "expect there will be a trade war."
However, uncertainty surrounding the issue continues to persist. On Monday, Trump complained about unfair car tariffs between the U.S. and China, referring to it as "STUPID TRADE."
(https://twitter.com/realDonaldTrump/status/983284198046826496)
China's foreign ministry spokesman, Geng Shuang, said trade tensions were the fault of the U.S. and that his country couldn't engage in negotiations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/the-us-is-making-trade-negotiations-impossible-says-chinas-foreign-ministry-report-2018-04-09) on the situation as it stands, according to Reuters.
Some investors were looking ahead to a speech by Chinese President Xi Jinping at the Boao Forum--the so-called Asia Davos (https://www.cnbc.com/2018/04/09/chinese-president-xi-jinping-may-announce-reforms-at-boao-forum-speech.html)--on Tuesday, in which he may make comments about market reforms that could ease tensions between the two countries.
See:Why China's Xi 'cannot back down' in trade battle with U.S (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/why-chinas-xi-cannot-back-down-in-trade-battle-with-us-2018-04-09).
With no first-tier economic data or Federal Reserve speakers expected Monday, those geopolitical issues may stay in the foreground.
Read:Republican senator on Trump's latest tariff threat: 'This is nuts' (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/republican-senator-on-trumps-latest-tariff-threat-this-is-nuts-2018-04-05)
In addition, traders will be watching developments out of Syria, after reports an air base near Homs, a city near Western Syria, was struck by missiles (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/airstrikes-hit-syria-state-media-says-but-us-denies-role-2018-04-08). The U.S. has denied any role in the strike, though Trump warned via tweets on Sunday that Syria and allies Russia and Iran would pay a "big price" for a suspected chemical-weapons attack on civilians near Damascus that left 49 dead over the weekend.
In another development on the geopolitical front, North Korea told the U.S. that leader Kim Jong Un is ready to talk about denuclearization (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/north-korea-willing-to-talk-denuclearization-us-says-2018-04-08), clearing a path for summit talks between Trump and the North Korean dictator.
Read:China tightens export restrictions to North Korea to comply with U.N. sanctions (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/china-tightens-export-restrictions-to-north-korea-to-comply-with-un-sanctions-2018-04-08)
What are strategists saying?
"Right now investors are learning how Trump operates in negotiating. He made an initial stance, trying to get the other side to cave in a bit, but recent commentary toward China has been more reserved and friendly, which is why we're higher today," said Sam Stovall, chief investment strategist of U.S. equity strategy at CFRA.
"However, investors remain rightfully concerned that this war of words could turn into an actual trade dispute that slows economic growth and accelerates inflation. There's no clear-cut signal for when we actually enter a trade war, and markets could still be disappointed about what could happen."
Which stocks are moving?
Gains in the technology sector were widespread. Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) climbed 2.2% while Alphabet Inc (GOOGL), the parent company of Google, was up 2.5%. Apple Inc(AAPL) rose 1.9%.
Shares of AveXIs Inc.(AVXS) surged 77% after Novartis AG(NOVN.EB) (NOVN.EB)said it would acquire the clinical-stage gene therapy group for $8.7 billion in cash (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/novartis-to-acquire-axexis-for-87-billion-in-cash-2018-04-09), or $218 per share. Novartis rose 0.9%.
General Motors Co.(GM)rose 1.3% after Morgan Stanley upgraded the automobile maker to buy.
Merck & Co.(MRK)rose 3.8% after the drugmaker said a cancer treatment met its primary endpoint (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/mercks-stock-surges-after-positive-keytruda-trial-results-2018-04-09) in a Phase 3 trial. The stock was one of the biggest gainers among Dow components.
AbbVie Inc.(ABBV)gained 3% after the company reported positive results (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/abbvie-shares-jump-22-on-news-of-positive-results-in-rheumatoid-arthritis-drug-trial-2018-04-09) in a late-stage trial of a treatment for rheumatoid arthritis.
Ionis Pharmaceuticals Inc.(IONS)gained 3.6% after the company's unveiling of a licensing deal (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ionic-pharmaceuticals-shares-jump-3-premarket-on-news-of-license-deal-with-astrazeneca-2018-04-09) with AstraZeneca PLC. U.S.-listed shares of Astra(AZN.LN)gained 0.9%.
At the same time, investors are looking ahead to the kickoff of the first-quarter earnings season on Thursday and Friday, when BlackRock Inc.(BLK), Wells Fargo & Co.(WFC)and JPMorgan Chase & Co.(JPM)are all due to report results.
What are other markets doing?
Asian stocks traded higher (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/asian-markets-waver-after-trumps-latest-broadside-against-china-2018-04-05), with the Hong Kong Hang Seng Indexrising 1.3%. European stockswere hitting two-week highs (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/european-stocks-rise-to-2-week-high-2018-04-09).
Gold futuresslipped 0.3% to $1,331.80 an ounce. The ICE U.S. Dollar Indexrose 0.14% at 90.237. Oil prices (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/oil-under-pressure-as-china-u-s-trade-battle-escalates-2018-04-06)shifted slightly higher, rising 0.3% to $62.24 a barrel, as investors kept an eye on Syrian airstrike news.
